notes.title: Firmware behaviour (modelled in WireLab)
lines: 1. K1 off at boot (SAFE).
2. After 1 s, close K1 and charge to the user set point (CHARGE).
3. Open K1 at set point - 3 V, predicted ahead by half a sample step plus the 10 ms relay release.
4. Hard cutoff: K1 open and FAULT latched above 310 V, in every state.
5. 30 s charge timeout -> FAULT; no rise past 30 V within 0.8 s -> FAULT (pen on work / short).
6. LCD: state bar, bank volts, stored joules, set point, bar graph, weld count, raw ADC mV.
7. Two-point ADC calibration constants (mv_lo/v_lo, mv_hi/v_hi) from meter readings.
READY keeps K1 open; a >= 20 V drop between samples counts as a weld -> HOLD 1.5 s -> recharge.
BOOT button: cycles the set point; clears a latched FAULT once the bank is under 310 V.

notes.title: Grounding
lines: U1 is non-isolated: PS1 -, the bank -, the pen and the ESP32 GND are ONE node.
PS1 must be floating. Never connect U2's USB to a PC while the bank is energized.
DCEN: pen (electrode) on -, work clamp on +.
Weld leads W1/W2 (12 AWG silicone, 600 V) solder straight to cap legs of opposite caps, never through board copper. Keep them short and twisted.

notes.title: Safety flags
lines: - Shock: with DCEN the clamp and the workpiece sit at +300 V against the pen, the ESP32 GND/USB-C shell, the power bank and PS1 -. Never hold the work in a bare hand while the bank is charged; the pen's metal pin vise is on the - node.

- The bank holds charge after K1 opens: bleed tau = 302 k x 190 uF = 57 s, so 300 V takes ~122 s to reach 36 V and ~4 min to reach 5 V. U1's own output capacitors (value unknown) are on the same node. Measure before touching.
- Discharge tool: 10 k across 300 V starts at 9 W and dumps 8.5 J (tau 1.9 s). Use a >=5 W wirewound or ceramic 10 k, not a 1/4 W part, and use it on U1's output too.
- U1 can reach 390 V but C1/C2 are rated 330 V: U1's pot is the only hardware limit. Set it to ~300 V unloaded, then lock it (glue or paint).

- Near the set point the bank rises ~500-700 V/s; at a 10 ms loop the relay cutoff overshoots 5-7 V. Sample fast (>=1 kHz) or keep the set point well under U1's pot setting. The 310 V cutoff is only 10 V above the 300 V ceiling.

- Board clearance: 2.54 mm pitch gives < 3 mm between neighbouring strips and between the + and - rails. A 300 V + rail beside the - rail breaks the 3 mm rule whatever the copper width (see the perfboard check).
- The underside C1+<->C2+ and C1-<->C2- jumpers each carry about half of the weld pulse (simulated peak ~1 kA total). Use 12 AWG or bend the cap legs together; thin jumper wire will fuse.
- Wire insulation on every 300 V jumper (blue, brown, U1 output) must be rated >= 300 V; silicone 600 V wire is the safe pick. Their gauges are not in the handoff.

- D1 (Vf ~0.6 V) clamps ADC_IN near 3.9 V, above the C6's 3.6 V absolute maximum. R5 limits the excess current to well under 1 mA so the pin survives, but a Schottky (BAT54/BAT85) clamps tighter, and the clamp current flows into the 3V3 rail.

- K1 must stay off while the C6 boots or resets: a GPIO's state is undefined until the firmware runs. A 10 k pull-down from K1.IN to GND (not in the BOM) makes that hardware-guaranteed. Also confirm the module switches reliably from 3.3 V.
- PS1 must truly float: check with a meter that PS1 - has no continuity to the plug's earth pin (many bricks tie it through the barrel or a Y-capacitor).
- 12 AWG weld leads are stiff: strain-relieve them so they do not lever the photoflash cap legs or their solder joints.
- There is no arm/disarm control: the modelled firmware charges automatically 1 s after boot. Consider a key switch or a long-press to arm.

notes.title: Open items (TBD - not guessed)
lines: - ADC GPIO for ADC_IN: free ADC1 pins on the C6-LCD-1.47 are GPIO0-3 (GPIO4/5 are the SD card, GPIO6 the LCD bus). The sim uses GPIO1.
- Control GPIO for K1.IN: free pads are GPIO0-3, 18-20, 23. The sim uses GPIO19. Check boot-time levels of the chosen pin.
- Confirm with a meter that U1's VIN- and VOUT- are internally common (the drawing ties both to GND, as the netlist does).
- R5 and D1 positions on the perfboard are not in the handoff. Suggested: run TAP (A/B/C18) to the ESP32 side and fit R5 + D1 beside the ADC pin.
- Exact holes for C1/C2 (rows 23-30) and the rail rows of the blue, green and U1 output jumpers.
- How U2 mounts on the F-J half, and where U2 GND meets the - rail.
- Gauges of the board jumpers and of the 12 V wiring (PS1 -> K1 -> U1 carries ~3 A while charging).
- Set-point input: not specified. The sim cycles presets 120/180/240/280 V with the BOOT button.
- Firmware margin, top-up and hold-off values are sim defaults (3 V, 8 V, 1.5 s), not requirements.
- Which cap takes the pen and which the clamp: the handoff only says opposite caps. Drawn: pen on C1 -, clamp on C2 +.
- Photoflash ESR, contact resistance and arc voltage are assumed model values; the simulated peak current scales with them.
- Retired: the salvaged disposable-camera flash booster is removed from every drawing.
